author: Khan Academy
description:
What if an assessment could ask a student "why?" and actually understand the answer?

We sat down with two members of Khan Academy's assessments team — Natalie McClurg
(former high school math teacher, now senior assessment content creator on the math team)
and Liz Rutkowski (longtime high school ELA teacher, now on the high school ELA assessments
team) — to talk about Khanductor and the new "Explain Your Thinking" item type inside
Khan Academy's new Interim Assessments.

Khanductor is a purpose-built, AI-powered conversation facilitator that appears only in
assessments. It stays content-neutral, works from rubrics written by our own math and ELA
content experts, and follows a traditional item with a short conversation — giving students
a chance to show what they actually understand, not just which answer they picked.

In this conversation:
• How "Explain Your Thinking" items are structured — traditional item, then conversation
• Why the conversation looks different in math vs. ELA
•
title: Don't Show Your Work. Explain Your Thinking. Introducing Innovative Assessments
